claims.text: The untreated eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical dual-phase lamellar-colony microstructure.
The untreated alloy has significant dislocation pile-ups at internal lamellar boundaries.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries produce local stress concentrations.
The local stress concentrations promote microcrack initiation and premature brittle failure during deformation.
The untreated alloy has high strength at room temperature.
The untreated alloy has poor room-temperature tensile ductility and brittle behavior.
Annealing below the recrystallization threshold can induce partial recovery in the alloy.
Partial recovery allows dislocations at internal boundaries to rearrange or annihilate.
Subcritical annealing can reduce the density of dislocation pile-ups at lamellar-colony boundaries.
A suitably controlled subcritical anneal can preserve the lamellar microstructure without appreciable coarsening.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups lowers local stress concentrations at internal boundaries.
Lower local stress concentrations decrease the likelihood of microcrack initiation during deformation.
Subcritical annealing will improve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
Subcritical annealing will retain the tensile strength of the untreated alloy.
Subcritical annealing may modestly increase tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
Extensive recrystallization or lamellar coarsening would reduce the alloy's strength.
The proposed performance benefit applies to room-temperature tensile loading and ambient service conditions.
